exposure: Implementation of an evidence-based labor induction protocol (standardized cervical ripening and early amniotomy)
outcome: Time from start of induction to rupture of membranes
Time from start of induction to delivery
Time from induction of labor initiation to vaginal delivery
cohort: The study included 887 patients who underwent induction of labor for a live singleton at >24 weeks' gestation, divided into groups before (387 patients) and after (500 patients) protocol implementation.
finding: The implementation of an evidence-based labor induction protocol was associated with decreased time to delivery, primarily due to a reduction in time to vaginal delivery among elective inductions, without negatively impacting other maternal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The protocol led to a shortened time from induction initiation to vaginal delivery for elective inductions and showed no difference in the cesarean delivery rate.
birth_weight: N/A (birthweight was similar in patients before and after protocol implementation, but not specified as an inclusion/exclusion criteria)
